finding: The variants emit unique NEGATIVE cluster_ids for un-hydrated unclustered context rows. The live query-map renderer indexes its COLORS palette with `(cluster_id % COLORS.length)`; JavaScript % truncates toward zero, so a negative id produces a negative index, COLORS[negative] is undefined, and the canvas silently ignores the invalid fillStyle. Every unclustered-shell point is painted in the colour of whichever point was drawn before it.
why_this_team_does_not_fix_it: Charter v1 non-duplication: this team writes no rendering code, no UI asset, no shader and no query.html, and touches no cluster colour. Rendering is owned by frontier-query-map-ui and product/static/query.html.
why_it_cannot_be_worked_around_on_the_va: Renumbering shells to a shared non-negative id would change what the frozen scorer sees: vendored metrics.structure() splits intra/inter pairs by cluster_id equality, so N distinct negative ids are treated as N singleton groups while one shared id would make every shell pair intra-cluster. That moves STRUCTURE_SEP and the frozen verdict. The charter forbids re-opening the scoring after the scores are seen.

amends.why_the_original_claim_is_incomplete: It states 'nothing else changes' for the rendering path. That holds for x, y, is_outlier and the cluster records, but the negative cluster_id is a NEW value class the page has never received, and one of its two palette lookups does not tolerate it. The original artifact is left byte-identical for provenance; this record is the correction.

minimal_fix_for_the_owning_lane: Change the point-fill index to a non-negative lookup, e.g. COLORS[((p.cluster_id??0)%COLORS.length+COLORS.length)%COLORS.length], or gate on the variant's own additive `unclustered` flag to paint shells in a declared neutral colour. Either keeps cluster colour decisions in the lane that owns them; this team makes no colour choice.
